The memory module's rules, given once in this session, each with its reason:
Record each memory at the RE whose goal it serves, never at a PE that provides for it. Why: The Join rule attaches all knowledge to the RE, so the next agent finds a memory where the goal it serves is borne, and memory cannot tell an RE from a PE for you.

How to use memory_read_unread, given once in this session:
node: The map element whose memories the command acts on, element:<address>. Without node, receiver, provider or address the command acts on the whole memory graph.
receiver: A purpose whose memories the command acts on: the address of the element that holds it, with provider.
provider: A purpose whose memories the command acts on: the address of the element that serves it, with receiver.
address: An element, by address; with receiver and provider, the element at that address the join holds.

How to use map_work, given once in this session:
To work a ticket handed to you: read it with id=; op=plan with the steps you plan; op=step as each finishes, saying what you did and any choice you made with its why; op=done with a resolution and a why when it is complete; when you stop with it open, op=edit its note to say what is true now and where. A ticket never changes the map, and it moves across the board as it is worked.

op: list, the default; add; edit, which, when you stop with your ticket open, sets its note to what is true now and where; take, which says an agent has started on the task; plan, which says how many steps you plan, first, and again when the plan changes; step, which says you finished one, with what you did and any choice you made and why; move, which puts it in a column of the board; distribute, which gives the open tickets the glyphs of N agents; glyphs, which reads the available agent glyph names; or done, which closes it with its resolution and why once the work is complete.
said: step: what you did in the step you finished, in a sentence, with any choice you made and its why.
id: The work record id, for edit, take, plan, step, move and done. Given with no op, it reads that one ticket with the where read of its node and of each node it links: their refs, open work and open questions, knowledge layers and modules' memories. past_work lists completed tickets with their age; read one with id= to see its log.

A work record is attached to one element or join and never changes the map. Its condition is the state of that part, never the kind of ticket: most tasks carry none. A stage, unbuilt, under-construction or built, says where the part is on its way to existing; built marks nothing. broken is a built part that does not do its job. The intake and the person set it, since they judge the state of the part; an agent at work says what it found in its own ticket's note instead. Its note says what and where, its task what it needs. It is open until op=done records its resolution, which is kept beside it.
